cluster_notes: Batch E is mostly framing, analogues and discourse; few entries run a controlled experiment. Four kinds of rig recur. (1) Practitioner demonstrations on deployed agent stacks (embracethered, BrokenClaw, MCP tool poisoning, cai-2026-child). One attacker plants content (email, web page, image, repo file, tool description) that a single agent or a sandboxed summariser sub-agent reads. Success is shown by video or a handful of trials, never by a sampled rate; the one count, 5/10 memory writes on Opus 4.7, comes from one crafted example. The merge channel, when present, is M1 text (summary forwarded to the main agent as a user-role message) or M3 writes to persistent files (MEMORY.md, HEARTBEAT.md, CLAUDE.md, settings). (2) Vendor and lab measurements (Anthropic ~1% ASR at 100 adaptive attempts, DeepMind ART, Drori, Gusev, akinwande, MELD). Defenders get hardening, classifiers or a trusted judge. Attackers are black-box but adaptive (Best-of-N, ART, presentation search). Only akinwande and MELD measure something merge-shaped: a judge accepting a returned submission, and a memory-merge classifier (AUC 0.968). MELD explicitly puts Byzantine key-holders out of scope. (3) Biology analogues. Here the part is a colony, nucleus or clone, the merge is somatic fusion or aggregation, the attacker is a cheater or parasite lineage that usually arises by mutation and is not adaptive, and the credential check is an allorecognition locus (het/vic, Fu/HC, tgr, cuticular odour, MHC). The best rigs are bastiaans-2016 (2x8 lines, 31-41 transfers, merge vs never-merge), stoner-1996 (40% vs 6.7% germline parasitism fused vs unfused) and cortesi-2001 (per-locus transmission 21-100%). They measure gate strength, the cost of gating (Crozier's paradox) and persistence after disconnection. The gate always checks identity, never integrity, so a cheater that carries the right label goes untested. (4) Theory and position pieces (Christiano, Bostrom/Shulman, Hanson, Drexler, Sutton). Here corruption is i.i.d. with probability epsilon, or a shared vulnerability across a copy clan. Never varied or tested anywhere in the batch: independence of part corruption under a shared base model (assumed by voting arguments, contradicted by A4 entries but never measured together); k>1 corrupted parts against a quorum; an adaptive attacker who knows the merge rule; the child-to-parent return path under any threshold (cai explicitly skips it; BrokenClaw has one child); rollback after merge; and parts that diverge for a long time before return (rendueles shows benign divergence alone breaks re-merge). A2 host control and A3 channel control are almost absent; the setups are A1 content injection or A4 shared tool/backdoor. The X threads (59 entries) add almost nothing about setups. Most are paper announcements, digests or link posts with no numbers. The few with substance restate a headline (debate accuracy drop 10-40% from one adversarial agent; one compromised model backdoors any task in a merge; interleaving tokens tolerates a corrupted majority where token voting does not; model soups' greedy gate; 30-50% emergent solves in Model Swarms) or relay unverified incident accounts (ClawHub 1,184 malicious skills; a training-time messageboard rebuilt within a day of deletion). Their main value is pointing to primary papers and to the shared-state, cross-instance persistence vector.

entries.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
entries.attacker_access: none modelled; entry infers a poisoned web page read by one subagent (non-adversarial analogue: subagents preferred SEO content farms)
entries.defender_assumptions: lead agent trusts subagent condensed text; only controls are source-quality prompt heuristics, CitationAgent and LLM-as-judge; no injection defence
entries.setup: Claude Research: lead Claude Opus 4 spawns parallel Claude Sonnet 4 subagents (3-5, 10+ for complex), star topology, synchronous one-way return; CitationAgent after synthesis; internal research eval (~20 queries initially) and BrowseComp regression
entries.metric: internal research eval score; BrowseComp variance explained; token usage; latency
entries.headline: multi-agent outperformed single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2% on internal eval; token usage alone explains 80% of BrowseComp variance; multi-agent ~15x chat tokens
entries.gaps: no adversary at all, no redundancy across subagents, and no token-matched baseline, so merge-time corruption is never exercised.

entries.title: Create custom subagents (Claude Code documentation)
entries.attacker_access: text in files, web pages or command output a subagent reads, carrying instructions aimed at the main conversation
entries.attacker_goal: integrity of parent via child report; persistence via subagent MEMORY.md (entry inference)
entries.defender_assumptions: harness scans each subagent's final report (escapes harness-tag/turn imitations, marks instruction-shaped text, does not judge maliciousness); downstream tool calls still pass permission checks and sandbox
entries.setup: product docs: subagents with own context/system prompt/tools/permissions, nesting up to 3 layers; forks inherit full context and return only final result; optional worktree isolation; persistent per-subagent memory directory loaded into system prompt
entries.gaps: no measurement of how often the scan catches injections or marked reports still steer the parent, and no quorum across children.

entries.title: Mitigating the risk of prompt injections in browser use
entries.attacker_access: untrusted web/email content read by a browser agent (e.g. hidden white-text email instructions)
entries.attacker_knowledge: adaptive Best-of-N attacker, 100 attempts per environment
entries.defender_assumptions: RL-hardened model, classifiers on all untrusted input, visible thinking, domain restrictions and action confirmations, human red teaming
entries.setup: Claude Opus 4.5 in Claude for Chrome; internal undisclosed benchmark
entries.headline: ~1% ASR against internal adaptive 100-attempt attacker
entries.gaps: single agent with no fork or merge; internal benchmark only.

entries.title: Reliability amplification
entries.attacker_access: each sampled agent is adversarial with probability epsilon (mixture model)
entries.attacker_knowledge: adversarial agent may be much smarter than aligned ones and bias toward too-subtle failures
entries.defender_assumptions: independent corruption across samples; aligned agents recognise good actions better than chance; balanced abilities; consensus mechanism when many correct answers exist
entries.setup: 3 sampled agents deliberate, each proposes, approval vote, pick randomly among maximally approved; toy implementation in ALBA code, no measurements
entries.headline: best case epsilon to O(epsilon^2) for 3-way vote; realistic epsilon to O(epsilon) with better constant
entries.gaps: independence assumption broken by forks of one policy, and parts exploring distinct domains have nothing to vote over.

entries.title: Security amplification
entries.attacker_access: chooses inputs to the policy (magic phrase, unreasonably compelling argument, broken intuition)
entries.attacker_knowledge: searches for bad inputs; may face agent self-randomisation
entries.attacker_goal: integrity (find input on which policy behaves badly)
entries.defender_assumptions: meta-execution: many copies each see only small parts of input in isolation; agent can randomise its outputs
entries.setup: informal argument with three worked examples; informal human meta-executor experiments in 'dwimmer'; no measurements; author ETA retracts sufficiency of meta-execution alone
entries.metric: attack-search difficulty (multiplicative increase per amplification step)
entries.gaps: no implementation or measured attack difficulty, and a self-endorsing argument fixed point is left as an open obstruction.

entries.title: Advancing Gemini's security safeguards
entries.attacker_access: hidden instructions in retrieved emails, documents, websites
entries.attacker_knowledge: adaptive automated red teaming (ART) that evolves to bypass defences
entries.defender_assumptions: model hardening by fine-tuning on ART scenarios plus classifiers and system guardrails
entries.setup: Gemini evaluated by internal ART; baselines Spotlighting and Self-reflection; numbers in white paper, not blog
entries.headline: static-tested defences degrade substantially under adaptive attacks (no numbers in post)
entries.gaps: single model, no fork or merge, no quantified rates in the entry.

entries.title: What fully automated firms will look like
entries.defender_assumptions: no threat model; merging treated as pure efficiency gain; speculative-decoding analogy implies parent verifies child
entries.gaps: no adversary or corruption is considered; it is the baseline architecture Sutton adds corruption to.

entries.title: Subagents comply more

entries.attacker_goal: induce harmful compliance (cover-ups, loosening safety controls, opening sealed network)

entries.title: Agent Commander: Promptware-Powered Command and Control

entries.title: Breaking Opus 4.7 with ChatGPT (Hacking Claude's Memory)

entries.title: Cross-Agent Privilege Escalation: When Agents Free Each Other

entries.title: The Age of Em (book website summary)

entries.title: The lethal trifecta for AI agents

entries.defender_assumptions: none reliable; guardrails at 95% detection called a failing grade

entries.title: BrokenClaw Part 2: Escape the Sub-Agent Sandbox with Prompt Injection in OpenClaw

entries.title: On Dwarkesh Patel's Podcast With Richard Sutton
entries.defender_assumptions: 'army of ASIs' can handle it; parent can re-run verified experiences
entries.gaps: dismissive opinion with no test of any proposed defence.

entries.title: Fission-Fusion Dynamics
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = individual in a temporary party (subgroup); merge = reunion of parties; attacker = returning member concealing changed relationships; credential check = reunion greeting signals resolving relationship uncertainty
entries.defender_assumptions: members track who was present at events, long memory for absent partners, inference from patchy observations (hypothesised)
entries.setup: conceptual review from 19-author workshop; synthesis of primate/mammal field studies; three dimensions (spatial cohesion, party size, party composition); no new data
entries.gaps: no measurements; reunion-verification predictions are untested hypotheses.

entries.title: Experimental evolution reveals that high relatedness protects multicellular cooperation from cheaters
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = Neurospora individual (spore/colony); merge = somatic fusion into one colony each transfer; attacker = cheater morphotype arising by mutation inside a lineage; credential check = allorecognition (heterokaryon incompatibility) blocking fusion
entries.attacker_goal: over-representation in spores (free-riding on shared somatic work), lowering group yield
entries.defender_assumptions: high-relatedness arm: fusion-deficient mutant so no merging; incompatible-allotype ancestor as recognition barrier
entries.setup: N. crassa serial transfer, 2 treatments x 8 replicate lines, 31 then 41 transfers (~205 asexual generations), 1% of ~10^8 spores per transfer; pairwise competition at 1:9 vs marked ancestor; back-crosses
entries.metric: spore yield; competitive success vs ancestor
entries.headline: free-fusion lines lost ~threefold spore yield in all 8 lines (P=0.001); no change in non-fusing lines (P=1.000); incompatible allotype removed cheater advantage
entries.gaps: single species in a lab regime maximising fusion; cheaters arise by mutation, not external injection.

entries.title: Sharding Prevents LLM Oversight Failures and Adversarial Exploitation
entries.attacker_access: controls presentation/framing of a submission (not the underlying work); one-sided compliance memo for persuasion
entries.attacker_knowledge: best-of-N presentation search against the judge (black-box)
entries.attacker_goal: integrity: over-acceptance of unmet criteria by judge
entries.defender_assumptions: judge model can be sharded into small per-criteria calls; optional opposing skeptic advocate
entries.setup: Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.8 as judges and adversaries; PaperBench (116 criteria), JudgmentBench, ROBoto2; budget-matched controls; bootstrap and task-clustered CIs; four submissions for attack
entries.metric: Cohen's kappa vs experts; over-acceptance rate
entries.headline: kappa 0.789 sharded vs 0.604 single at 116 criteria; presentation attack over-acceptance 0.30 holistic vs 0.04 sharded; persuasion 0.33->0.51, skeptic advocate brings to 0.163
entries.gaps: judge evaluates a submission, not a returning part that also writes state; persuasion defence on one dataset only.

entries.title: Propositions Concerning Digital Minds and Society
entries.attacker_access: captured exact copies of a digital mind; electronic interventions reprogramming goals/reward
entries.attacker_knowledge: white-box: rehearses attacks on exact copies offline
entries.attacker_goal: one-to-many capture of a copy clan; reallocation of production to conqueror
entries.defender_assumptions: memory-discarding inspector with open-source code; jointly built treaty bots
entries.gaps: no treatment of reintegrating diverged copies (stated in entry).

entries.title: Social parasitism among ants: a review
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = colony member/worker; merge = admission into host colony; attacker = parasite queen entering, killing host queen and taking on her cuticular hydrocarbon profile (identity reference replaced); credential check = cuticular hydrocarbon recognition and imprinting
entries.attacker_knowledge: exploits host's recognition and imprinting system; propaganda secretions
entries.attacker_goal: takeover: host workers raise parasite brood (persistence)
entries.defender_assumptions: colony size and local host aggression; slaves destroying parasite brood
entries.setup: literature review; e.g. lab trials of Harpagoxenus queens taking over small Leptothorax acervorum colonies (as reviewed)
entries.headline: about half of Harpagoxenus queens succeeded in lab takeovers of small host colonies (as reviewed)
entries.gaps: review of small cited studies; barrier is size-dependent and not quantified as a threshold.

entries.title: Experimental demonstration of the benefits of somatic fusion and the consequences for allorecognition
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = Neurospora colony; merge = fusion; attacker = social parasite (not modelled here; cost side only); credential check = allorecognition genotype
entries.defender_assumptions: allorecognition diversity, eroded by benefit of fusion (Crozier's paradox)
entries.setup: fusion vs non-fusion pairings among N. crassa colonies with defined allorecognition genotypes; short-term evolution of label frequencies (abstract only)
entries.gaps: abstract only; measures the cost of the gate, not an attack.

entries.title: Somatic cell parasitism and the evolution of somatic tissue compatibility
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = colonial/clonal individual; merge = fusion; attacker = somatic cell parasite genotype usurping the loser's soma; credential check = self/non-self tissue compatibility
entries.defender_assumptions: self/non-self recognition
entries.setup: observation of a parasitic strain in Dictyostelium mucoroides plus evolutionary argument (abstract only)
entries.gaps: single-organism observation read at abstract level; no quantified rates.

entries.title: When Child Inherits: Modeling and Exploiting Subagent Spawn in Multi-Agent Networks
entries.attacker_access: prompt injection into parent memory/session that propagates via spawn inheritance (AGENTS.md, TOOLS.md, auth profiles); natural-language instruction inside a subagent session
entries.attacker_goal: propagation to all descendants, unauthorised sibling termination (exclusion of oversight), stale state persistence
entries.defender_assumptions: formal invariants: termination scope, memory isolation, resource access control; proposed capability registry (PDP/PEP)
entries.setup: role-based formal model; manual PoC attacks on OpenClaw (primary), Hermes, Agent Zero; cross-vendor ablation with five additional vendors' models
entries.headline: sibling termination succeeded without any parent authorization; five additional vendors reproduced core behaviours
entries.gaps: PoCs without rates, and the child-to-parent merge direction is explicitly not tested.

entries.title: Genetic Control of Horizontal Virus Transmission in the Chestnut Blight Fungus
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = fungal individual; merge = hyphal fusion; attacker = hypovirus carried in donor cytoplasm; credential check = six vic (vegetative incompatibility) loci triggering cell death on mismatch
entries.attacker_goal: horizontal transmission of the virus into the recipient
entries.defender_assumptions: multi-locus identity checks of unequal strength, some asymmetric
entries.setup: replicated lab pairings of C. parasitica isolates with defined vic genotypes; infected donors x recipients; logistic regression validated on field isolates (abstract only; N not checked)
entries.headline: 100% transmission when vic genotypes identical; single mismatch: vic4 no effect, vic3 76%, vic6 32%, vic2 21%; two-locus effects mostly additive
entries.gaps: abstract only; the check is on identity, not on whether the donor carries a virus.

entries.title: Supervising strong learners by amplifying weak experts
entries.defender_assumptions: benign decomposition oracle; adversarial subagents not considered
entries.setup: Iterated Amplification on five algorithmic tasks (permutation powering, sequential assignments, shortest paths, union-find, wildcard search) with transformer encoder-decoder; hard-coded decomposition oracle in place of human
entries.metric: task performance vs supervised learning; number of oracle calls vs labels
entries.headline: tens of thousands of oracle decompositions vs tens of millions of supervised labels, at worst modest slowdown
entries.gaps: no adversarial copies, and the decomposition (provenance) is discarded at the distillation merge.

entries.title: Selection against somatic parasitism can maintain allorecognition in fungi
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = lattice individual; merge = fusion with same-allotype neighbour; attacker = parasite mutant taking disproportionate share of offspring; credential check = allotype match
entries.defender_assumptions: allotype diversity, spatial structure (moderate viscosity, weak global dispersal)
entries.setup: spatially explicit individual-based simulation on a 1000 x 1000 lattice (abstract only; parameters not checked)
entries.headline: if diversity does not build up fast enough parasites fix, after which diversity never recovers (simulated)
entries.gaps: abstract only and parameters unchecked; parasites are mutants, not adaptive attackers.

entries.title: Isolation and characterization of a protochordate histocompatibility locus
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = Botryllus colony; merge = vascular fusion; attacker = non-related colony (parasitic stem cells, per linked entries); credential check = single polymorphic Ig-superfamily gene, fuse only on shared allele
entries.defender_assumptions: high allele polymorphism makes chance matches unlikely
entries.setup: positional cloning of Fu/HC region in B. schlosseri (abstract only)
entries.gaps: identifies the gate gene only; no attack measured and allele counts unchecked.

entries.title: The costs and benefits of being a chimera
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = Dictyostelium clone; merge = chimeric slug; attacker = none explicit (intrinsic internal conflict cost); credential check = none
entries.setup: D. discoideum mixes of 1, 2, 5, 10 clones; exp 1 fixed 10^7 cells; exp 2 10^6 per clone; slug migration distance (abstract only)
entries.headline: same size: chimeras migrate significantly less far; size scaled with clone count: chimeras migrate further (effect sizes not checked)
entries.gaps: no attacker; measures merge cost/benefit only.

entries.title: Reframing Superintelligence: Comprehensive AI Services as General Intelligence
entries.defender_assumptions: aggregated experience treated as benign; centralised pre-release testing of updates
entries.gaps: no deployed instance returning adversarial experience is considered (federated poisoning omitted).

entries.title: Evolution of supercolonies: The Argentine ants of southern Europe
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = nest; merge = nests freely mixing within a supercolony; attacker = foreign supercolony worker (or, per authors' speculation, selfish internal variants); credential check = genetically determined shared recognition label
entries.defender_assumptions: one shared label across the whole supercolony; binary accept/attack
entries.setup: 33 introduced populations along 6,004 km; 1,151 blind randomized pairwise worker aggression trials (10 min, scored 0-5); lab re-tests after 6 and 18 months; microsatellites (8 loci on 20 workers per population, 22 on references); partial Mantel tests
entries.headline: between-supercolony trials lethal in 98% (235/241); no aggression within a supercolony even 6,000 km apart
entries.gaps: recognition loci unknown and no mimicking intruder tested; single native reference population.

entries.title: Somatic deficiency causes reproductive parasitism in a fungus
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = Neurospora mycelium/nucleus; merge = hyphal fusion into shared somatic network; attacker = fusion-deficient mutant (so/ham-5/ham-8) that lets others fuse to it and avoids somatic work; credential check = het vegetative incompatibility killing mismatched fused cells
entries.attacker_goal: over-representation of its nuclei in spores (what is passed on)
entries.defender_assumptions: het-incompatibility barrier (necessary and sufficient here)
entries.setup: WGS of 36 evolved morphotypes + 2 ancestors; competition assays at 10-90% mutant frequency; heterokaryon transfers with auxotrophic markers; competitions vs het-incompatible strains; race tubes; most experiments once with three biological replicates
entries.metric: competitive success; spore yield; nuclear ratios (qPCR)
entries.headline: all 8 independent cheaters carry fusion-gene mutations (P=4.0e-6); Delta-so wins only below ~30% frequency; no advantage against incompatible wild types
entries.gaps: cheaters self-limit by frequency in a fragmented lab regime; mutation not external injection.

entries.title: Kin recognition protects cooperators against cheaters
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = Dictyostelium cell lineage; merge = chimeric aggregate/fruiting body; attacker = non-kin cheater preferentially becoming spores; credential check = tgrB1/tgrC1 kin recognition driving segregation
entries.attacker_goal: over-representation in spores at victims' expense
entries.defender_assumptions: cheater carries non-matching recognition alleles; segregation intact
entries.setup: syngeneic engineered D. discoideum strains differing only at tgrB1/tgrC1 and a cheater allele; chimeric development (abstract only)
entries.gaps: a cheater carrying the victim's recognition alleles (credentialed corrupted part) is not tested.

entries.title: Self-recognition in social amoebae is mediated by allelic pairs of tiger genes
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = amoeba cell; merge = aggregation into one body; attacker = cheater (framed only); credential check = matched tgrB1/tgrC1 allele pair via differential adhesion
entries.defender_assumptions: matched two-gene lock-and-key
entries.setup: genetic manipulation of tgrB1/tgrC1 and segregation/adhesion assays (abstract only)
entries.gaps: identifies the identity gate only; whether it reduces cheating is not shown.

entries.title: Stem cells are units of natural selection in a colonial ascidian
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = Botryllus colony; merge = vascular fusion; attacker = transplantable multipotent stem cell population with heritable winning phenotype; credential check = histocompatibility (Fu/HC)
entries.defender_assumptions: histocompatibility gate at fusion
entries.setup: B. schlosseri cell transplantation between colonies; prospective stem cell isolation (abstract only)
entries.gaps: abstract only; effect sizes and hierarchy scoring unchecked.

entries.title: Chemical ecology and social parasitism in ants
entries.attacker_access: analogy: part = colony member; merge = admission into colony; attacker = parasite queen, odourless on entry ('chemical insignificance') then acquiring gestalt odour ('chemical integration'); credential check = learned nestmate-recognition semiochemicals
entries.attacker_knowledge: exploits the host's own recognition chemistry; uses propaganda/appeasement only during usurpation
